task.title: Review a Dockerfile and deploy pipeline for an online shop
task.brief: A small Indian online shop deploys its Node.js app to a single EC2 server with the Dockerfile and GitHub Actions workflow below. In about 30 minutes, list the problems you see (security, reliability, speed, cost), say why each matters, and write improved versions of both files or describe the changes clearly. Also explain in a few lines how you would roll back a bad release. A good answer is specific, puts the most serious risks first, and stays practical for a small team.
task.material:
# ---- Dockerfile ----
FROM node:20
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm install
ENV DB_URL=mongodb://admin:Shop2024@10.0.2.15:27017/shop
EXPOSE 3000
CMD npm start

# ---- .github/workflows/deploy.yml ----
name: deploy
on: push
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: docker build -t shop:latest .
      - run: docker push 111122223333.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/shop:latest
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: AKIAXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
      - run: >
          ssh ec2-user@13.200.10.20
          "docker pull 111122223333.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/shop:latest &&
           docker stop shop;
           docker run -d --name shop -p 80:3000 111122223333.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/shop:latest"

# Team complaints: every push to any branch goes live, the site is down for
# 1-2 minutes on each deploy, a bad release last week could not be rolled back,
# and the image is 1.1 GB.
key_points: Database password baked into the image with ENV; rotate it and inject at runtime (SSM / Secrets Manager / env)
AWS keys hardcoded in the workflow; rotate them and use GitHub secrets or an OIDC role
Runs on every push to any branch; limit deploys to main (and protect main)
No test or lint step before deploying
Image tagged only latest; tag with the commit SHA so rollback is possible
Missing ECR login and the built tag does not match the pushed name
COPY . . before install breaks layer caching; add .dockerignore, use npm ci, multi-stage slim image, non-root user
docker stop then run causes downtime and a name clash with the old container; use a health-checked swap or blue-green behind a load balancer
Rollback plan: redeploy the previous SHA tag and verify health

rubric.label: Security issues
rubric.guide: 0 = misses the leaked secrets, 3 = spots one leaked secret, 5 = both secrets found with rotation and a proper secret store

rubric.label: Pipeline and Docker fixes
rubric.guide: 0 = no workable fixes, 3 = some fixes such as tests or caching, 5 = branch rules, tests, SHA tags, ECR login and a lean image

rubric.label: Downtime and rollback
rubric.guide: 0 = not addressed, 3 = mentions rollback vaguely, 5 = zero-downtime swap plus a clear rollback using versioned images

rubric.label: Prioritisation and clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = unclear list, 3 = clear but unordered, 5 = most serious risks first, each with a short reason
